intro.title: Forms & Validation
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a user registration form with real-time validation feedback that checks email format, password strength, and required fields. You'll learn how Angular's reactive forms work using FormBuilder and FormControl to manage form state and user input. The lesson covers implementing built-in validators like required and email, creating custom validators for complex rules, and displaying dynamic error messages that update as users type. You'll use Angular's FormGroup to organize form controls, subscribe to value changes for real-time validation, and apply conditional CSS classes to show validation states. By the end, you'll have a fully functional form that provides immediate user feedback and prevents invalid submissions.
intro.usecase: Forms and validation are fundamental to virtually every web application, from user registration and login screens to complex data entry forms in enterprise software. You'll find these patterns in e-commerce checkout flows, contact forms, survey builders, CRM systems, and admin dashboards where users input customer data or product information. Professional applications require robust client-side validation to provide immediate feedback, reduce server load, and improve user experience by catching errors before submission. Angular's reactive forms with built-in validators are essential for building scalable applications that handle user input reliably, whether it's a simple newsletter signup or a multi-step wizard for financial applications.
